sso.description: Let your team sign in to Marble with your company identity provider (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace…). Settings apply to all your organizations.
sso.domains.added: Domain added. Marble verifies it before it is used for sign-in.
sso.domains.description: Users whose email ends with one of these domains are sent to your identity provider when they sign in. Domains you add stay pending until Marble verifies them. Contact support to change or remove a domain.
sso.domains.empty: No domain yet. Add the email domains your team signs in with.

sso.enable.description_locked: Available once a test sign-in succeeds. When off, the configuration is kept and users sign in with email and password.
sso.enable.description_off: When off, the configuration is kept and users sign in with email and password.
sso.enable.description_on: Users from your sign-in domains are now redirected to your identity provider. Uncheck to switch back to email and password.
sso.enable.description_recovery_key: First create a recovery key for this organization below and confirm you stored it, so you can turn SSO sign-in off if a configuration change locks you out.

sso.license_missing: Your licence does not include SSO.
sso.offline_access.missing: Without the offline_access scope, users may be asked to sign in again at every session. Some identity providers keep users signed in by default; otherwise add offline_access to the scopes above, if your provider supports it.
sso.recovery.confirm.description: This key will never be shown again. Without it you can't turn SSO sign-in off if a configuration change locks you out.
sso.recovery.confirm.title: Did you store your key?
sso.recovery.copy_now: Copy this key now. For security reasons it will never be shown again: store it in your password manager.
sso.recovery.create_card.description: The key is shown only once: store it in your password manager. If a configuration change locks you out, use it with the commands below.
sso.recovery.create_card.title: Create a recovery key
sso.recovery.description: If a configuration change locks you out, a recovery API key lets you turn SSO sign-in off through the public API and sign back in with email and password. Create it now and keep it somewhere safe.
sso.recovery.errors.forbidden: You don't have permission to create API keys.
sso.recovery.example.description: Run this from a terminal with curl and jq, with MARBLE_API_KEY set to your key. It reads the current configuration and saves it back with SSO sign-in off, so your team can sign in with email and password while you fix it. When IP allowlisting is on, run it from an allowed IP address.
sso.recovery.example.title: Example: turn SSO sign-in off if you are locked out
sso.recovery.none: This organization has no recovery key yet. Without one, a broken SSO configuration can lock everyone out. Create one below before you enable SSO sign-in or change its configuration.
sso.recovery.title: Emergency access
sso.recovery.update_example.description: Run this from a terminal with curl, with MARBLE_API_KEY set to your key. The call replaces the whole configuration: send every field, as a field you leave out is reset to its default. The one exception is client_secret: leave it out to keep the stored secret. The command is filled with your saved configuration, without client_secret; with no saved configuration, replace the placeholder values before you run it.
sso.recovery.update_example.fields.clien: Required. The client ID of the Marble app in your identity provider.
Optional. Leave it out to keep the stored secret. Required for a new configuration and when issuer or client_id changes.
sso.recovery.update_example.fields.email: Optional. The ID token claim that holds the user's email. Empty or left out, Marble reads email.
sso.recovery.update_example.fields.extra: Optional. Extra parameters added to the authorization request, as key-value text pairs. Left out, they are removed.
sso.recovery.update_example.fields.issue: Required. The issuer URL of your identity provider. It must start with https://.
sso.recovery.update_example.fields.scope: Optional. Defaults to openid, profile and email. Add offline_access to keep users signed in, if your identity provider supports it.
sso.recovery.update_example.fields.sso_e: Always send it: left out, it turns SSO sign-in on. true sends users from your sign-in domains to your identity provider; false lets them sign in with email and password.
sso.recovery.update_example.title: Example: update the whole configuration
